research.topic: First modern Olympic Games: Athens, 6–15 April 1896, opened in the Panathenaic Stadium (ancient stadium rebuilt in white marble, paid for by Georgios Averoff); 241 athletes from 14 nations, 43 events, all male; first women at Paris 1900 (22 women). First champion James Connolly (USA), triple jump, 6 April 1896, who had left Harvard to compete. Marathon (first ever) ≈ 40 km from Marathon to the Panathenaic Stadium, 10 April 1896, won by Spyridon Louis, a Greek water carrier, in 2:58:50.

myths.myth: The modern Olympics began in Paris, home of their founder Pierre de Coubertin.
myths.reality: Coubertin founded the IOC in Paris in 1894, but the first Games were held in Athens in April 1896; Paris hosted the second Games in 1900.

landscape.our_gap: Olympic history clips are either long documentaries or trivia lists; nobody counts the 241 athletes, erases 'any women' and runs the first marathon route into the marble stadium on a moving map as a quiz.
